subject: Private observability export — proposal for SIEM ingestion (BankCorp)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>, LogScale Onboarding <onboarding@logscale.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private observability export — proposal for SIEM ingestion (BankCorp)

Samir — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. I put together a short proposal for how Redwood can deliver logs/traces/metrics from a VPC/private deploy into BankCorp's SIEM with the constraints you outlined (no persistent outbound sockets to public third parties, encrypted signed bundles for air-gapped transfer, and retention policy alignment).

High level proposal (two-mode):
- Real-time forwarder (preferred where allowed): a lightweight forwarder running in the customer VPC that pushes only pre-filtered, tokenized events to a LogScale HEC endpoint over mTLS to a dedicated ingestion proxy in BankCorp's DMZ. Only metadata+non-PII tokens leave the VPC.
- Periodic evidence bundles (airgap/air-gapped sites): for environments that cannot accept any outbound connections, the forwarder writes signed export bundles (gzipped JSONL + index) to a mounted secure NFS or S3-compatible bucket inside the customer's network. BankCorp retrieves bundles using a signed manifest and verifies signatures prior to ingest.

Security & compliance controls:
- Field-level redaction with a customizable policy enforced in the forwarder (PII detection + hashing).
- Signed export manifests (Ed25519) and per-bundle checksums for chain-of-custody.
- Audit header injection: each event includes routing metadata and a non-replayable nonce.

Operational notes / ask from BankCorp:
- Confirm whether BankCorp has an on-prem HEC/LogScale listener (IP address, cert CA) for real-time ingestion.
- If using periodic bundles, confirm the retrieval cadence and the transport mechanism (scp, vault-agent pull, or secure courier).

Attachments: sequence diagram and checklist attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync (30m) to validate whether BankCorp will accept mTLS HEC or needs bundle-only.
2) If mTLS allowed, we’ll share an engineered runbook and a small PoC container for the forwarder (2 week lead).

If you want, we can also include a short eval harness that demonstrates redaction effectiveness on a sample dataset.

Thanks,
--
Priyom Das
Solution Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-forwarder-sequence-diagram.png (image/png), evidence-export-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Chang <laura.chang@bankcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability export — proposal for SIEM ingestion (BankCorp)

Thanks, Priyom — thoughtful write-up. A few clarifying questions from our security and legal reviewers: 

1) PII / PHI handling: can the forwarder guarantee deterministic redaction prior to any outbound transmission? We need an auditable transform (not just hashing at the forwarder) — ideally we want a redaction report per bundle.
2) Chain-of-custody validation: our compliance team requires an HSM-backed signing key for any evidence bundles. Do you support HSM key references or would we run the signing key locally (customer-managed)?
3) Retention alignment: if the forwarder writes to an S3-compatible store, how do we ensure lifecycle TTLs map to BankCorp's retention (90 days for generative-model-derived artifacts)?

Finally, for sites that are strictly air-gapped we will almost certainly go bundle-only and use a secure courier. Please include an example manifest format and the retrieval verification steps in the runbook.

Can Kimberly and Marcus be looped in to confirm the technical constraints?

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Security Engineering, BankCorp
samir.patel@bankcorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability export — proposal for SIEM ingestion (BankCorp)

Samir — great questions. A few technical clarifications and commitments from Redwood: 

1) Deterministic redaction and reporting:
- The forwarder can run an auditable transform pipeline: each bundle includes a redaction manifest that lists fields transformed along with rule ids, deterministic salt (customer-provided), and a sample checksum. We will include a "redaction-report.json" in each bundle that your auditors can validate against the bundle-level checksum.

2) HSM-backed signing:
- We support referencing customer-managed HSM keys via PKCS#11 or a KMS URI (Azure Key Vault / AWS CloudHSM / on-prem HSM gateways). For the PoC we can ship a reference implementation that signs locally; production will use the customer's HSM (we will not hold private keys).

3) Retention mapping:
- The forwarder includes object lifecycle metadata on the bundle (x-redwood-retention: 90d). If pushing to an S3-compatible store inside the customer's network, lifecycle enforcement is the customer's responsibility. We will include a pre-built lifecycle policy template for common S3-compatible systems in the runbook.

Manifest example (excerpt):
- manifest.json:
  {
    "bundle_id": "string",
    "created_at": "RFC3339 timestamp",
    "signer": "key-id or KMS uri",
    "files": [{"path":"events.jsonl.gz","sha256":"..."}],
    "redaction_report": "redaction-report.json"
  }

I’ve attached the sequence diagram and checklist. Marcus — can you confirm the forwarder's resource footprint and whether we can ship a small mode that performs only metadata-level forwarding to support strict PII policies?

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Product Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: egress-forwarder-sequence-diagram.png, evidence-export-checklist.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability export — proposal for SIEM ingestion (BankCorp)

Thanks — quick notes from implementation: 

- Forwarder sizing: small mode (256MB RAM, single vCPU) supports metadata-only extraction (timestamps, event_type, hashed_id) and writes bundles at ~20MB/min under normal load. Full mode (2GB RAM, 2 vCPU) supports field-level redaction and gzip+index. PoC will default to small mode.
- HSM integration: we’ve validated PKCS#11 flows against SoftHSM for testing; production integration requires your on-prem HSM team to provide the signing key handle and the KMS URI.
- Manifest & verification: our verifier will accept either a signed manifest (Ed25519) or a manifest signed by an HSM-backed cert chain. We also support signed/immutable indices for increased assurance.

Next steps (I’ll own the PoC):
1) Schedule a 30m runbook review (I can run through the manifest format and verification steps).
2) We’ll provision a PoC forwarder container and a small sample dataset (non-prod scrubbed) for you to exercise redaction/reporting.

I'll send a calendar invite; Priyom will coordinate the artifacts.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
